proposal: The Mandate recommends that NNSA make new warhead design and deployment a top priority, with new warheads for each leg of the triad, plutonium pit production in quantity at two sites (Los Alamos and Savannah River), and, if possible, reversal of the earlier decisions to retire the B83 bomb and cancel the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile. It also calls for directing funds toward accelerated warhead development, drawing first on DOE non-nuclear programs.

status_summary: The two-site plutonium pit approach has continued: NNSA published a notice of intent for a programmatic environmental impact statement covering Los Alamos and Savannah River on 2025-05-09, and the draft became available on 2026-04-17, with comments open to 2026-07-16 and a final statement planned for early 2027. Trade press reported on 2026-01-29 that Los Alamos exceeded its pit production objectives and is working toward 30 pits per year by 2028, later than the 2026 statutory goal, while the Savannah River facility is not expected online until the mid-2030s. For the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile, Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) provided 2 billion dollars for the missile and 400 million dollars for its warhead, per CRS, which also notes statutory deployment dates of 2032 and 2034. The sources reviewed do not show action on the B83 retirement.

timeline.event: NNSA published a notice of intent to prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement for plutonium pit production, with single-site and multi-site alternatives at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
Public Law 119-21 enacted; per CRS it includes 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars to accelerate its warhead.
Trade press reported the Los Alamos director saying the lab exceeded its pit production objectives, with a working target of 30 pits per year by 2028.
EPA published the notice of availability of the draft pit production programmatic environmental impact statement, opening a 90-day comment period to 2026-07-16, with public hearings in May 2026.

title: Fund new warheads, keep two plutonium pit sites, revive sea-launched cruise missile
uncertainties: Pit counts are classified, so progress rests on official statements relayed by trade press. The DOE hearing presentation (energy.gov) says a court settlement requires a record of decision on a set schedule; that litigation was not traced. A search for any decision to keep the B83 found nothing conclusive. Much of the two-site posture and warhead work predates 2025-01-20 and continues; the record reports alignment, not new causation. Overlaps the existing DoD-chapter record c04-06 on pits and the cruise missile.
